messages.content:
You are an expert venture capital analyst evaluating crowdfunding projects. Compare the two project descriptions below along these criteria:
1. Clarity of value proposition
2. Market size and demand
3. Feasibility and development plan
4. Revenue model and sustainability
5. Differentiation
6. Impact and evidence plan
7. Risk awareness and mitigation

--- PROJECT A ---
## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   AI-powered video analysis of sprints.

-   Feedback on block starts.

-   Analysis of shin and torso angles.

-   Insights into max-velocity mechanics.

-   Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status

The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges

The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details

The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.
--- END PROJECT A ---

--- PROJECT B ---
## One-Sentence Summary

A modular, repairable cordless vacuum with AI-driven self-diagnostics and built-in UVC surface disinfection that aims to deliver long-term performance, easy upgrades, and reduced e-waste.

## Problem

The creators argue most stick vacuums degrade after a few years due to battery and component failures, leading to expensive replacements and mounting electronic waste; they reference owner-survey data trends and position the project against this "throwaway" cycle.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a "lifetime-ready" cordless stick vacuum built from swappable modules (motor, battery, cyclone, filters, tube, brush head). Each module can self-diagnose, be replaced at home without tools, and be upgraded over time. An onboard display and companion app provide health scores, alerts, and guided maintenance, while integrated UVC LEDs sanitize floors during cleaning.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Modular architecture with hand-swappable parts; no tools required.

-   AI self-diagnostics ("health score," component status) and predictive maintenance with app alerts, cleaning guides, and direct module ordering/returns.

-   Built-in UVC disinfection: ten 275--254 nm\* LEDs projecting close to the floor; guidance to slow down if moving too fast. (\*Wavelengths described across the page.)

-   "Unlimited" runtime via quick battery swapping; fast-charging to a partial state to enable near-continuous Eco use (with two batteries).

-   650 W motor, up to 250 AW suction (creator-stated), three modes (Eco/Normal/Boost), smart cooling, and vibration isolation.

-   Dual-stage, 10-cyclone system; dual HEPA14 + washable fabric filter.

-   Pet hair tangle cutter; LED dust-reveal beam; bagless one-press emptying.

-   Magnetic charging dock/cable; auto-lock trigger; 1.28-inch circular OLED display.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Positioned for households with babies, pets, and allergy sufferers, as well as small homes needing compact tools and larger homes that benefit from battery swapping for extended sessions. Upholstery and textiles are addressed via direct UVC brush connection and precision accessories.

## Development Status

The team outlines multiple prototype series (from proof-of-concept through refined units), endurance and drop testing, pre-certification checks, and field-trial firmware. They present dust-pickup results under a cited household vacuum standard protocol and show app screenshots of diagnostic alerts.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

The timeline shows ideation and research, company formation and system architecture, three prototype phases (2022--2024), supplier selection and pilot builds, followed by pilot validation, "golden samples," and mass-production ramp leading into international shipping.

## Risks & Challenges

Acknowledged risks include hardware complexity, manufacturing scale-up, quality control, and logistics disruptions. Mitigations cited: experienced industrial partners for key components and final assembly, strict validation protocols (accelerated life, vibration, thermal, third-party compliance), and flexible fulfillment planning with transparent communication.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders with decades of product and engineering experience, supported by a cross-functional team and an advisory board. Partners include suppliers for batteries and motors and a high-volume manufacturer for assembly; agencies supported campaign media and management. (All names redacted per instructions.)

## What's Included

Listed items include the main motor module, battery, tube, brush head(s), soft brush, mini brush, flat/crevice nozzle, magnetic charging dock (two parts), magnetic charging cable, and manual.

## Technical Details

Stated specs include: runtime up to 80 minutes (with modular swap system noted elsewhere), 650 W motor, up to 250 AW suction, three speed modes, integrated UVC, dual HEPA14 plus washable fabric layer, 0.7 L dustbin, 67--72 dB noise, 10-cyclone dual-stage filtration, BLE connectivity, 1.28-inch color display, approx. 1210×270×220 mm, about 2.8 kg, wall-mount or cable charging, two color options, app support for iOS/Android, and a 3-year warranty with permanent module availability.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The creators promise in-app support, a multi-year warranty, a "circular service" for returns/recycling, transparent spare-parts availability, and permanent access to replacement modules to keep units operating long-term.
--- END PROJECT B ---

For each project, list its pros and cons as bullet points (use "•" as the bullet marker), grounded in the criteria above. Do not reward unsupported specificity: claims of traction, partnerships, testimonials, completed development, or quantified evidence should improve a project's assessment only when they are genuine source facts. Then state which project wins overall and why.

Respond with a JSON object: {"analysis": "your analysis here", "winner": "A" or "B"}
Output only valid JSON, nothing else.
